title: Nila Campus Books Grant — Punjab eligibility
text: Nila Campus Books Grant. This fictional test scheme reimburses undergraduate college textbooks for students living in Punjab. The applicant must be enrolled at a public college, be aged 18 to 25, and have monthly family income at most 12000 rupees. It does not pay hostel rent or tuition fees. Approval requires verification.

title: Nila Campus Books Grant — application
text: Nila Campus Books Grant application procedure. Punjab students submit their college enrolment certificate, residence proof, family income certificate and textbook receipts at the district education office. Applications close on 30 September in this fictional test scheme. Eligibility conditions are recorded in the separate eligibility section.

title: Uday Diploma Fee Support — Bihar
text: Uday Diploma Fee Support is a fictional Bihar scheme paying tuition fees for technical diploma students at government polytechnics. Students must reside in Bihar and have annual family income below 180000 rupees. The scheme covers course fees, not textbooks or hostel accommodation. Submit admission proof and an income certificate to the polytechnic principal.

title: Sanjeev Kidney Care — Maharashtra
text: Sanjeev Kidney Care is a fictional Maharashtra programme covering recurring dialysis sessions for low-income residents with chronic kidney disease. A nephrologist referral and residence certificate are required. Treatment is offered at empanelled hospitals. It does not cover cataract surgery or routine dental work. Approval requires medical review.

title: Nayan Eye Surgery — Tamil Nadu
text: Nayan Eye Surgery is a fictional Tamil Nadu programme offering cataract operations to residents aged 60 and above. An ophthalmologist must confirm cataracts that impair vision. The programme covers surgery and follow-up examination at approved eye hospitals. Dialysis and kidney treatment are excluded.

title: Aashray Roof Repair — Delhi
text: Aashray Roof Repair is a fictional Delhi housing programme paying to repair leaking or storm-damaged roofs of owner-occupied homes. The homeowner must reside in Delhi, own the property and have annual household income under 240000 rupees. Renters, new house purchases and mortgage interest payments are excluded. Apply at the municipal housing office with ownership documents and damage photographs.

title: Saksham Mobility Aid — Haryana
text: Saksham Mobility Aid is a fictional Haryana programme supplying wheelchairs and walking aids to residents with certified locomotor disability of at least 40 percent. It supplies assistive equipment rather than a cash pension. Applicants need a disability certificate and assessment by an authorised rehabilitation specialist.

title: Shramik Accident Relief — Punjab
text: Shramik Accident Relief is a fictional Punjab programme providing a one-time compensation payment to registered construction workers injured at work. The worker must have registered with the construction welfare board before the accident. Hospital records and an accident report are required. The programme does not provide a recurring old-age pension.

title: Sandhya Senior Pension — Bihar
text: Sandhya Senior Pension is a fictional Bihar programme paying a monthly old-age pension to residents aged 65 or older with no other government pension. Applicants need age proof, residence proof and a bank account. Registration as a construction worker is not required. Compensation for workplace injuries is outside its scope.

title: Silai Artisan Toolkit — Punjab
text: Silai Artisan Toolkit is a fictional Punjab programme supplying sewing machines to women who complete certified tailoring training and intend to work from home. It supplies equipment, not a business loan. Applicants provide a training certificate and proof of Punjab residence. It does not pay college tuition or textbooks.

title: Bazaar Vendor Credit — Maharashtra
text: Bazaar Vendor Credit is a fictional Maharashtra programme offering repayable working-capital loans to licensed street vendors for buying stock and operating small stalls. Applicants must hold a valid vending certificate. It is a loan rather than a free grant or pension. Tailoring machines and agricultural irrigation equipment are outside its scope.

title: Boond Farm Irrigation — Haryana
text: Boond Farm Irrigation is a fictional Haryana programme reimbursing part of the cost of drip irrigation equipment for small farmers. Applicants must own or lease agricultural land in Haryana and submit land records, supplier quotations and installation receipts. Domestic roof repairs and urban street vending are not covered.

title: Vidya Hostel Assistance — Delhi
text: Vidya Hostel Assistance is a fictional Delhi programme helping low-income college students pay approved hostel accommodation charges. The student must study at a recognised Delhi college and live in a registered student hostel. Submit enrolment proof, an income certificate and hostel fee receipts. Textbook purchases and tuition fees are excluded.

title: Poshan Mother Nutrition — Bihar
text: Poshan Mother Nutrition is a fictional Bihar programme providing nutrition packages and antenatal check-ups to pregnant residents registered at a public health centre. Applicants provide pregnancy registration and residence proof. The benefit is food and prenatal care rather than student support or an old-age pension.

title: Neer Fisher Boat Repair — Tamil Nadu
text: Neer Fisher Boat Repair is a fictional Tamil Nadu programme helping licensed small-scale fishers repair storm-damaged fishing boats. The fishing vessel must be registered locally. Applicants submit vessel registration, fishing licence and repair estimates. Domestic house roofs and farming irrigation equipment are excluded.
